summary: Rate-limit heatmap request and guidance for custom refill/window smoothing to avoid short spikes
description:
Issue summary: BrightCart (dedicated) is asking for two things: 1) a visual heatmap in the Console showing token consumption by refill window over time so they can identify microburst hotspots, and 2) concrete guidance and option to configure a custom smoothing/refill window per-tenant to avoid short-lived 429 spikes during mixed realtime + bulk embedding workloads.

Customer note: They run a hybrid ingest pipeline: a continuous realtime chat surface (~5qps) plus intermittently scheduled bulk embedding batches (concurrent workers). They observe occasional identical short 429 spikes across many API keys in the org during batch start times even though overall token usage is under committed capacity. They want to both understand the traffic pattern (visual) and be able to reduce the short spike exposure without sacrificing steady throughput.
impact: Intermittent 429s for a small percentage of chat flows during scheduled embedding job starts. Customer reports user-visible chat timeouts ~0.1-0.5% during batch kicks which impacts SLAs for certain pages. No billing discrepancies reported.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer schedules concurrent embedding worker job (200 parallel workers) to start at 02:00 UTC.
2) At the same time, realtime clients continue to send chat requests.
3) Observed behavior: a cluster of 429 responses for short windows (3-6s) immediately after batch jobs start.
4) Staggering the batch start by 30s reduces, but does not eliminate, the short bursts.
logs_and_traces: Attached: sample trace IDs from BrightCart (trace: bc-20260310-1, bc-20260310-2), token_bucket_refill Grafana panel link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rl_windows/token_bucket_refill?org=brightcart, sampling of request/response headers showing X-RateLimit-* for affected requests (pasted in comments).
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Logged with SRE and assigned Diego. Requested sample API keys, traces, and approximate batch start schedule.
Customer (BrightCart) 2026-03-10: Provided traces and schedule. Confirmed they're on a dedicated pool with reserved capacity and using default tenant smoothing settings.

SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-11: Initial hypothesis: refill window alignment across edge proxies may be creating transient double-accounting when large fanouts happen at near-same second boundaries. Requested edge proxy logs and NAT mapping table snapshot for the batch start time.

SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-11: Also asked engineering to check token-bucket refill algorithm and rounding behavior for short windows. Added link to internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/RateLimit+Debug+Runbook.
Customer (BrightCart) 2026-03-11: Asked if Redwood can temporarily increase burst window for their tenant to avoid user-facing errors while we investigate.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12: Confirmed temporary burst increase is possible as a stopgap. Scheduled a maintenance config change for 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC with planned rollback if no improvement.
SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-12: Post-change note: short spikes reduced by ~85% in sampled window; still observed rare 429s when batch workers start with <5s skew.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Refill alignment skew at the edge. Our token refill runs on a 1s tick; edge proxies with slightly different clocks cause multiple requests to be counted in adjacent buckets leading to transient double-throttle signals.

Hypothesis B: HTTP/2 multiplexing and connection reuse from pooled proxies can cause per-connection accounting to be misattributed when worker fanout occurs, slightly amplifying the token draw in origin accounting.

Data: Grafana panel shows refill histogram spikes at 02:00:01 and 02:00:02 UTC with a tight cluster of high token consumption events. NAT table snapshot indicates 14k concurrent connections re-used by the bulk upload workers across 6 proxy nodes at start time.

Finding: Edge proxies were configured with a 250ms clock lead relative to origin, causing some refill events to be applied earlier at the edge. Combined with worker fanout starting within the same second, earliest requests are occasionally counted twice during the alignment window. This is amplified for dedicated customers using pooled proxy IPs and HTTP/2 multiplexing.

Temporary mitigation applied: increased tenant burst window to +50% for 24 hours and enabled a per-tenant smoothing flag on the rate-limiter. Observed ~85% reduction in user-facing 429s for the sampled job run.

Root cause summary: refill tick alignment + connection pooling + high-concurrency job start produces transient accounting artifacts that manifest as short 429 spikes for realtime flows overlapping batch starts.
Metrics and links: token_bucket_refill histogram, request qps overlay, and edge-proxy-clock-drift panel (links attached above).
resolution: Short-term workaround: Increased tenant burst allowance and enabled per-tenant smoothing. Customer to stagger batch starts by >=10s for best results until console visualization rollout.

Medium-term remediation: Engineering to add a 'refill-heatmap' panel to Console showing per-refill-window token usage (work started, PR referenced). This will let customers see microburst hotspots and choose smoothing windows intentionally.

Long-term fix: Scheduler change to make refill alignment origin-driven (single authoritative tick) and to add configurable per-tenant smoothing/refill-window sizes in the Console. Follow-up epic planned: INT-22098 (rate-limiter: per-tenant window config + UI).

Follow-up items: (1) Add a KB article for hybrid workload best practices and recommended smoothing settings; (2) Run a short experiment to enable origin-driven refill alignment for 10 dedicated tenants and measure effect; (3) Ensure documentation of recommended embed-worker start jitter in Quickstarts.

Status: Temporary config applied 2026-03-12; medium-term Console panel PR merged to staging. Customer confirmed reduced user impact and requested Console ETA - target Q2 2026 for GA of heatmap feature.
